text: The placement is issued through the one published write operation of the service, POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions (API-S9-002) on /api/recovery/partner/v1 with Partner portal right C and the Idempotency-Key header, and no path of its own; the legacy story names only the two reads API-S9-001 and API-S9-003, so the write is taken from TSD S9 T-A.1 and the two reads are declared by the baseline and built by the panel and instruction stories.
why: The legacy Endpoints table gives two GETs and no operation that places an account, and the FSD describes the placement as a user action on a screen. TSD S9 T-A.1 publishes exactly one operation that issues an instruction, with right C and first in E4, so declaring a new path would invent an interface and leaving the act without an operation would leave the feature unbuildable.
read: TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD S9 A2.6.2; legacy RWB-E6-034 Endpoints; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-13 and R5.4 class H
applied_in: RWB-S9-E6034-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 7, 12.1, 13 and 19; RWB-S9-E6034-CON sections 2, 3, 7 AC1, 12.1 and 19
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-partner tech lead, before the contract is tagged
impact: Both stories build the placement behind the published operation, and a build that adds a path fails the contract review

text: The placement result, its rule version and the agency the allocation picked are recorded on the local decision record through DP-03 and not on partner_instruction, because no column of the table carries them; the record is written before the instruction is sent, no column and no migration is added, and partner_user is declared as an owned table without a field catalog because no source gives one.
why: TSD S9 T3.1 gives partner_instruction nine fields and none is a rule version, a rule ID, a decision reference or a pick evidence, and it gives partner_user no object definition at all. Adding a column or a field ID would be a business value invented by the builder, and dropping the rule version would leave legacy AC1, which asks for the decision log with the rule version, unsatisfiable.

text: The placement rule is read as data at its version in force from rwb-decision and is expressed by the D9 rows R-WO-29 to R-WO-32 of the Write-off route set, because S9 owns no route set of its own; the agency is the one the measured-return allocation of FEAT-PRM-03 picks, the version is recorded with the placement, and the absent DP-04 rows RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and RWB-P7-E1073-CON are tracked rather than declared.
why: The routing logic carries ten route sets and no partner set, and its States sheet marks PLACEMENT_DECIDED a decision point and PLACED_WITH_AGENCY a partner step of the Write-off set; the FSD names FEAT-PRM-03 as the prerequisite and the row R-WO-30 places the account with the agency chosen on measured return. DP-04 is not in the pattern set the plan gives this key, and the rule package registry is rwb-decision by the default ruling.

No source gives a payload field list or a consumer set, and DP-09 is absent from the pattern set, so both are recorded rather than invented.

text: The case and its post charge-off state are read on the rwb-case contract and never as a recovery_case row, and the D9 states PLACEMENT_DECIDED and PLACED_WITH_AGENCY stay with the write-off route set: this story issues the instruction against a case reference, writes no case row and no case state column, and records the two consumed rows as absent from the plan C row.
why: The FSD existing-capability check reuses the case record and the shared entities through the P3 interfaces, and the D9 states are states of the Write-off route set whose owner column names business roles and systems, not services. Writing a case state from rwb-partner would break DP-01 and the case ownership, and skipping the case read would place an account on a case that is not post charge-off.

text: The issue is authorised on the Partner portal right C taken from TSD S9 T-A.1 and T6.1: seven identities hold C (RW-AGENCYMG with CRUDA and the six CRU roles), the legacy permission table right R for the eight roles it names and 21 more resolves to the fifteen further staff roles and the six PT-* identities of the matrix, 29 in all, and the FSD also-uses role Credit Administration officer has no matrix row and therefore no right until the access owner adds one.

Taking the legacy right alone would leave the feature unbuildable, and granting a new row would invent an access decision, so the matrix is taken and both conflicts are recorded.
